nodes.summary: For `L ≤ G`, base `x` is covered by exactly `k` reads for `N.choose k * L ^ k * (G - L) ^ (N - k)` of the start tuples.
nodes.title: Exact depth law (count form)

nodes.summary: For `L ≤ G`, base `x` is uncovered by all `N` reads for exactly `(G - L) ^ N` of the `G ^ N` start tuples.
nodes.title: Exact coverage count

nodes.summary: A read of length `L` starting at position `s` of a circular genome of length `G` covers base `x` when `x` is one of `s, s + 1, …, s + L - 1 (mod G)`, i.e. `(x - s) mod G < L`.
nodes.title: Read covering a base of a circular genome

nodes.summary: The depth of coverage of base `x`: the number of reads covering it.
nodes.title: Depth of coverage of a base

nodes.summary: For `0 < G` and `L ≤ G`, the expected number of reads with no successor is `N (1 - (L - 1) / G) ^ (N - 1)`. The `0 < G` hypothesis is essential: at `G = 0` and `N > 0`, the right-hand expression is `N` while the sum of totalized normalized counts is zero.
nodes.title: Expected number of no-successor reads (exact)

nodes.summary: Read `j` has no successor when no other read starts in the `L - 1` positions after it, `starts j + 1, …, starts j + L - 1 (mod G)` (reads starting at the same position are not successors of each other). In Lander and Waterman's terms such a read is counted as ending an island, but several no-successor reads can lie in one island, so this is not the island count.
nodes.title: Read with no successor

nodes.summary: The depth at a fixed base is binomial with `N` trials and success probability `L / G`, for `L ≤ G`.
nodes.title: Exact depth law

nodes.summary: `normalizedCount` agrees with Mathlib's totalized uniform measure on all start tuples. This measure is a probability law only when the sample space is nonempty.
nodes.title: Normalized count agrees with the totalized uniform measure

nodes.summary: Exact uncovered probability (Clarke–Carbon, Lander–Waterman, circular genome): `(1 - L / G) ^ N` for `L ≤ G`.
nodes.title: Exact uncovered probability

nodes.summary: The totalized normalized count `|E| / G ^ N` of a set of start tuples. For `0 < G`, this is the probability when the `N` start positions are independent and uniform on `Fin G`. If `G = 0` and `N > 0`, the sample space is empty and this value is zero, so it is not a probability law. For `N = 0`, there is one empty start tuple, even when `G = 0`.
nodes.title: Normalized count of read start tuples

nodes.summary: For `L ≤ G`, summed over the reads, the number of start tuples in which read `j` has no successor is `N * G * (G - (L - 1)) ^ (N - 1)`. This counts no-successor reads, not island ends: a start tuple can have several no-successor reads in one island.
nodes.title: Count of no-successor reads (exact)

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of `tendsto_normalizedCount_uncovered`, the probability that a given base is covered by exactly `k` reads tends to `e^{-c} c^k / k.factorial`.
nodes.title: The coverage depth tends to Poisson(`c`)

nodes.summary: With read length `L` fixed, genome lengths `G N ≥ L`, and coverage `N L / G_N → c` as the number of reads `N → ∞`, the probability that a given base is uncovered tends to `e^{-c}`.
nodes.title: Lander–Waterman limit for the uncovered fraction

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
